newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha prices rise on overseas crude rally.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha prices rise on overseas crude rally.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices jumped in afternoon trade on Monday, supported by a rally in overseas crude prices on Friday, traders said.

Offers for second-half July open-spec naphtha were heard at $216.00 per tonne, while bids were notionally assessed at around $215.00. It was sold to a South Korean oil firm at $213.00 in late Friday trading.
First-half August was quoted about 50 cents higher than second-half July.
Inter-month spreads were little changed, with second-half July/second-half August quoted at minus $1.50/minus 50 cents.
Physical naphtha trading in July cargoes has yet to get into full swing amid ample prompt supplies, traders with petrochemical producers said.
"We are quite relaxed as we know quite a few near-term cargoes are readily available in the market," one trader said.
In term talks, Abu Dhabi National Oil Co (ADNOC) asked three of its Japanese jet A-1 term lifters to submit by May 21 their bids for a one-year supply contract starting July.
Initial bids are likely to be lower than the current premium of 75 cents as some recent spot deals were believed to have been done at premiums of 10 to 20 cents, traders said.
